CROSS-CAMPAIGN REPRODUCIBILITY, MEASURED PRECISELY. Against the superseded turn-grain receipt, the OFF arm reproduces on ALL SEVEN per-question graded metric dicts (session_recall@k, evidence_recall@k, reader_surface@k, reader_evidence@k, turn_recall@k, evidence_retrieved@k, chunk_evidence_recall@k) AND pool_size on 20/20 questions - but its full ordered ranked_ids list differs on 4/20 (S1 2311e44b, a11281a2, 1f2b8d4f; S2 4adc0475). Two of the four differ inside the top-5: 2311e44b is a PURE REORDER of the same five ids and a11281a2 is a MEMBERSHIP change (s37:t10 in, s23:t2 out); the other two first differ below the top-5 (indices 6 and 15). So 'byte-identical' holds at the METRIC level only, never at the ranking level, and the base retrieval RANKING is itself unstable across campaigns. For the injected arms the graded metrics differ on exactly three (arm, question) cells: inj_only and on on S2 3c1045c8 (each session_recall@5 and evidence_recall@5 0.5 -> 1.0), and on on S1 4f54b7c9 (reader_surface@5 1.0 -> 0.5, aggregate 0.95 -> 0.90). The residual is therefore NOT confined to the injected arm - it is harness-side and affects OFF too.

REPRODUCIBILITY PROBE ON THE DIVERGENT CELL (S2 3c1045c8 — the divergence that MOVES A GRADED METRIC in the direction the work claims; it is TWO of the three divergent (arm, question) cells, and the third, on/S1 4f54b7c9, is a reader_surface@5 regression that is NOT separately diagnosed here, so the 'not a code effect' attribution below applies to 3c1045c8 only). The divergence is a SEED-ORDER difference, not a code effect: the two campaigns' seeded_sessions lists hold the SAME 5 sessions in a different order (positions 2/3 swapped), and the seed order is first-seen pool rank, so the base pool's ORDER at the C4 insertion point differed even though the graded metrics are identical. THREE single-question artifacts were produced at this revision: TWO barrier-on runs and ONE barrier-off re-run; all three give session_recall@5 1.0, and the barrier-off run's ranked_ids are byte-identical to both barrier-on runs. An AST-level (docstrings stripped) comparison of session_reinjection.py between the two revisions confirms the barrier is the ONLY executable change IN THAT FILE (the same commit also changed the test files and run.py's argparse help strings, none of which the arms execute), so the barrier is result-neutral and the divergence is harness-side (the eval's pre-sort pool order is not pinned).

FULL-SAMPLE REPEATABILITY AT THIS REVISION (evidence, not a caveat). The whole S2 injection-only arm was re-run TWICE independently (fresh graphs, same cohort, same flags, seedless checkpoints): the @5 metrics (session_recall@5, and therefore recall_all@5 / evidence_recall@5) are identical on 10/10 questions in BOTH repeats, and the second repeat is byte-identical in the top-5 ORDER on all 10. The first repeat changes the top-5 ORDER on 2 questions (f35224e0, 60036106) with the id set unchanged - f35224e0 moves 4 of the 5 indices, 60036106 moves 2. The DEEPER movement is not uniform and is NOT part of the repeatability claim: IN REPEAT 1, f35224e0 also moves evidence_recall@20 and turn_recall@20 (0.5 -> 1.0 each, versus the main arm) and reader_evidence@20 and evidence_retrieved@20 with them, while REPEAT 2 is identical to the main arm at @20 on all 10 questions. context_tokens moves in repeat 1 on f35224e0 (7064 -> 7009) and 60036106 (7986 -> 8000), and in repeat 2 on 7405e8b1 (7997 -> 7984). The no-change guarantee is @5 ONLY.

ARM ISOLATION IS A PER-QUESTION WIPE, NOT ONE DB PER ARM. The docker:// URI's path is the BASE graph name, which the eval's per-question namespace (team_default__default__<qid>) overrides — so the three arms share graph NAMES on the :6399 server and the runner script's GRAPH.DELETE <dbbase> is a no-op. Effective isolation comes from run.py's gated per-question wipe (MATCH (n) WHERE n.lme_question_id = $q DETACH DELETE n) followed by a full re-ingest; ingest_latency_ms of 27-84 s per question per arm confirms the re-ingest actually happened (no cache hit). A refused wipe (live/stale run marker) would leak the previous arm's state; no marker file was present in the arm work dirs, so the wipe ran. Recorded because the superseded receipt claims 'ONE DB PER ARM', which is not what the mechanism does.

PROCESS-LEVEL LATENCY IS NOT A COST PROXY IN THIS CAMPAIGN. The machine was under fleet load: OFF-arm retrieval latency is 110.2 ms (S1) / 90.8 ms (S2) here versus 69.4 / 57.7 ms in the superseded receipt on IDENTICAL code. Use the ISOLATED C4 block cost (session_reinjection_stats.latency_ms = fetch + annotate + merge only) for the arm's cost: 6.4-9.0 ms mean per arm, worst single question 26.0 ms.

The dedicated :6399 instance was used because the shared :6379 instance was at its 512 MB maxmemory cap (writes failed) and :6380 was concurrently in use by another test lane (its logs show an active defrag on foreign graphs). :6380 and :6379 runs aborted with ingest OutOfMemoryError / health-check failures; their reports are NOT used.

Turn points have no per-turn index property, so the fetch's deterministic order for turns is coalesce(lme_chunk_index,-1) = -1 for every turn, then p.id LEXICOGRAPHIC (t0, t1, t10, t11, ... t2). The injected turn SET is therefore deterministic but not chronological. Unchanged from the shipped order clause; recorded.
The injected turn points are NOT clawed back by the C5 chunk re-cap (dedup_pool counts only is_raw_chunk hits), so the total budget is the only injection-volume guard at the default grain.

1_flip_census.verdict: MECHANISM SURVIVES; BYTE-IDENTITY DOES NOT. At turn grain the guard-ablated top-5 is not byte-identical to OFF (S1 7/10 questions identical, S2 10/10). EVERY id that enters the top-5 is a BASE item already present in OFF's ranked pool (2/2 membership changes; the remaining diffs are pure reorders) - ZERO injected items enter hits[:5] without the guard. So the injected items are the TRIGGER (they fire the guard), not the entering items. The ablated arm's own metric contribution is sample-dependent: inj_only is +0.10 recall_all@5 on S1 and 0.00 on S2, +0.05 pooled, so a single-sample reading would credit the guard with a swing that is not there. This is also the falsifier most exposed to the harness residual recorded under acknowledged_limitations: the S2 question 3c1045c8 does not reproduce across campaigns because its seed ORDER differs. (In THIS receipt the 3 OFF-vs-inj_only top-5 differences are all S1; 3c1045c8 was one of the 2 S2 differences in the SUPERSEDED campaign.)

revision_measured.verified_by: tools/longmem_eval/guard_measured_revision.py (committed 807e0ad02 and hardened in later commits — `git log --oneline -- tools/longmem_eval/guard_measured_revision.py` is the authority on that history, and this field is written by one of them, so it names none of them) — `python -m tools.longmem_eval.guard_measured_revision --rev c1e6f7f2d --paths tortoise/ tools/` from this worktree exits 0, reporting 255 files compared, ONE comment/docstring-only difference (tortoise/retrieval.py), the files added after the revision (this guard tool: it did not exist at that revision, so it is listed, not compared), and 100 byte-cache files, which the guard NOW REFUSES by default — see BYTECODE below (that historical check ran under the superseded default that excused them). It refuses, with the reason on stderr, when: the revision does not resolve or any git call fails; a file present at the revision is deleted or no longer tracked; a tracked .py differs executably (docstrings and comments stripped before the AST comparison); a tracked non-.py differs at all; a tracked file's MODE or on-disk TYPE changed (a chmod -x, or a regular file replaced by a symlink of the same bytes, executes differently while the content compare passes); a non-allowlisted untracked file exists under the surface; or nothing under --paths existed at the revision, because an empty comparison must not read as a clean one. It does NOT read git diff, so assume-unchanged/skip-worktree index flags, rename collapsing and .gitignore rules cannot defeat it — all three were demonstrated as bypasses against the previous implementation and are now refused. STATED LIMIT: the excused set is by SUFFIX only, never by directory, so a stray __pycache__/evil.py refuses. BYTECODE (#3712, closed in this branch): a .pyc is executable code and CPython runs it in preference to the .py beside it, and a forged byte-cache's mtime/size header matches its source by construction — so no header check can separate it, and one crafted __pycache__/evilmod.cpython-312.pyc executed different code while the superseded default printed 'no executable change'. The guard now REFUSES any .pyc/.pyo under the surface BY DEFAULT — untracked, staged/index-tracked, committed, or present at the measured revision alike, case-variant suffixes included (the match is casefolded — on a case-insensitive filesystem the importer's ...cpython-312.pyc open() resolves to a forged ...PYC, which the cycle-14 review reproduced executing while the guard exited 0): git's bookkeeping does not change what CPython executes, and the first fix (which scanned only the untracked set) was itself defeated by an INDEX-tracked forged byte-cache reported as 'added after the revision' with the guard still exiting 0. The former --strict-bytecode flag is the default (kept as a no-op), and the measured run is required to be byte-code-free: tools/longmem_eval/run_protocol.py launches every run step with -B and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 (for the runner and the children it spawns). --allow-bytecode is the explicit opt-out, and a run that takes it states in its own output that the attestation does NOT cover bytecode. For the historical verification above this means the 100 excused byte-cache files would now produce a REFUSAL: re-running the attestation requires the byte-caches cleared (or the opt-out taken, with the weaker claim recorded). The declared bypass surface is pinned by tests/test_guard_measured_revision.py (58 tests, one per declared class: content drift, index flags, rename collapsing, ignore rules, mode/type, presence, non-Python files, unresolvable revision, git failure, empty surface, byte-cache refusal by default — untracked, staged, committed, present-at-revision and case-variant suffixes each pinned — and the declared exemptions). Out of its scope, by construction: reachability (it proves absence of executable change on the declared paths, not that a change sat on the executed path, and not that the declared paths are the entire import graph; the measured command also imports tests/model_adapters.py lazily for a non-default ingest mode, which is outside the declared surface)
